transcript: so I finally saw the Titanic musical after almost a decade of being infatuated with the score and it didn't disappoint in case you don't know Titanic won the Tony Award for Best Musical in 1997 the same year that the James Cameron film came out but the two are totally unaffiliated with each other This production at encores has an absolutely stacked cast of musical theater professionals including Ramin Karimloo Bonnie Milligan Brandon Uranowitz Judy Kuhn, Chip Zien and many many more including by the way all three Coopers the score of this show aside from being just stunningly beautiful is also incredibly well integrated into the book Maury Yeston wrote these just brilliantly crafted and brilliantly conceived musical sequences and scenes that honestly just blow my mind like I feel like I could write an essay on some of the individual numbers the book is definitely very different from the James Cameron movie it's much more of like a panoramic snapshot of the Titanic showing it as kind of a microcosm of society not just in terms of the diverse group of people but also how the ship and its downfall encapsulated so much about like the hubris of capitalism and all that and I could understand someone seeing the show and feeling like that's all well and good but it's kind of difficult to invest in the individual character arcs. I did feel that way a little bit in Act 1 but even then I honestly didn't care like there were still moments in Act 1 where I started crying just because I was so moved by the fact that I live in a world with such beautiful music in it. but then we got to the lifeboat sequence in Act 2 and I genuinely started sobbing and I realized that I was invested in these characters and that these few scenes that we had gotten with each of them to learn about their hopes and their dreams and their relationships it was enough of a hook that that when it all just crumbles like a house of cards and then for the rest of the show to watch them just look death in the eye it's devastating so all of that to say I left the show emotionally shattered and awed by this display of artistry so if you can see it at encores before it closes this Sunday the 23rd I highly recommend it
